content:
Hi all!

We're designing a introduction + bootcamp workshop to train talented math students on the basics of Lean 4 and prepare them as reviewers of AI-generated Lean code, with the goal of producing Mathlib-ready output. Two questions: (1) What are the most common quality failures you see in AI-generated Lean that a trained reviewer should catch? (2) Has anyone tried a structured reviewer training program and what was the minimum time to usefulness?

Thanks,
Raj
@Rajarshi Maiti, have you been in touch with @Yaël Dillies about the reviewer bootcamp (non-AI-focused) that they are organising. You may be able to share materials.

Rajarshi Maiti said:

We're designing a introduction + bootcamp workshop to train talented math students on the basics of Lean 4 and prepare them as reviewers of AI-generated Lean code, with the goal of producing Mathlib-ready output. Two questions: (1) What are the most common quality failures you see in AI-generated Lean that a trained reviewer should catch? (2) Has anyone tried a structured reviewer training program and what was the minimum time to usefulness?

Re your (1): at the moment the "definition" of Mathlib-quality Lean 4 code is mostly tacit knowledge. It is hard to write down precisely. Most of it is based on intuition that people in the community have gained through years of hard work building Mathlib.
The best way we have right now of communicating this knowledge is by collaborating intensively with experts in the community.
